norse_idunn.name: keeps and dispenses the apples that hold off the gods' old age
norse_idunn.notes: Snorri's Skáldskaparmál names her keeper of the apples the Æsir bite to ward off old age until Ragnarök; her loss to Þjazi causes the gods to wither.

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda), 'Bragaræður'/ch. on Iðunn

norse_idunn.name: restores the youth of the aging gods
norse_idunn.notes: The apples she guards renew the Æsir's youth; without her the gods grow grey and old (Haustlöng; Skáldskaparmál).

norse_jord.name: is the personified Earth, the ground itself
norse_jord.notes: Snorri's Gylfaginning and Skáldskaparmál treat Jǫrð as the Earth personified, daughter of Nótt, mother of Thor by Odin; she is the land and soil.

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning and Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda)

norse_jord.name: bears Thor, the defender of the worlds, to Odin
norse_jord.notes: Thor is repeatedly called Jarðar burr ('son of Jǫrð'); she is among the foremost ancestresses of the Æsir.

norse_nanna.name: dies of grief at Baldr's death and follows him onto the pyre
norse_nanna.notes: Gylfaginning: when Baldr is laid on Hringhorni, Nanna's heart breaks with grief and she dies and is burned beside him.

norse_nanna.name: sends gifts back from Hel to Frigg and Fulla
norse_nanna.notes: From Hel she gives Hermóðr a linen robe for Frigg and a finger-ring for Fulla to carry back to the living.

norse_rindr.name: bears Váli, the one-night-old avenger of Baldr, to Odin
norse_rindr.notes: Baldrs draumar foretells that Rindr will bear Váli in the western halls; the child avenges Baldr at one night old.

sources.reference: Baldrs draumar (Poetic Edda); Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning

norse_ymir.name: his slain body becomes the substance of the world
norse_ymir.notes: From Ymir's flesh the earth was made, from his blood the sea, from his bones the mountains, from his skull the heavens, and from his brains the clouds (Vafþrúðnismál; Grímnismál; Gylfaginning).

sources.reference: Grímnismál 40-41 and Vafþrúðnismál 21 (Poetic Edda); Snorri, Gylfaginning

norse_ymir.name: engenders the race of frost-giants from his own body
norse_ymir.notes: As he slept, a man and woman grew from under his arm and his two feet begot a son; thus the hrímþursar (frost-giants) descend from Ymir.

norse_thjazi.name: takes the shape of a great eagle
norse_thjazi.notes: In eagle-form Þjazi forces Loki to deliver Iðunn and seizes her with her apples (Haustlöng; Skáldskaparmál).

sources.reference: Þjóðólfr of Hvinir, Haustlöng; Snorri, Skáldskaparmál

norse_thjazi.name: abducts Iðunn and her apples, withering the gods
norse_thjazi.notes: His theft of Iðunn ages the Æsir until Loki recovers her; pursuing, Þjazi is burned and killed at Asgard's walls.

norse_magni.name: possesses prodigious strength even as an infant
norse_magni.notes: At three nights old Magni alone lifts the giant Hrungnir's leg off the fallen Thor, when no other god could move it (Skáldskaparmál).

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda), the Hrungnir episode

norse_magni.name: inherits Mjǫllnir and survives Ragnarök with his brother
norse_magni.notes: Vafþrúðnismál: Móði and Magni shall possess Mjǫllnir when Vingnir (Thor) falls in the renewed world.

norse_modi.name: embodies battle-courage and wrath (his name means 'Courage/Wrath')
norse_modi.notes: Móði ('the angry/courageous one') is named among Thor's sons; the name itself denotes martial fury.

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda), kennings for Thor

norse_modi.name: inherits Mjǫllnir and survives Ragnarök with Magni
norse_modi.notes: Vafþrúðnismál foretells that Móði and Magni will wield their father's hammer in the world after Ragnarök.

norse_vali.name: grows to manhood in a single day to avenge Baldr
norse_vali.notes: Vǫluspá and Baldrs draumar: Váli, son of Odin and Rindr, neither washes his hands nor combs his hair until he has brought Baldr's slayer to the pyre, at one night old.

sources.reference: Vǫluspá 32-33 and Baldrs draumar (Poetic Edda); Snorri, Gylfaginning

norse_ve.name: with Odin and Vili slays Ymir and shapes the world
norse_ve.notes: Gylfaginning: the three sons of Borr — Odin, Vili and Vé — kill Ymir and fashion the cosmos from his body.

norse_ve.name: gives the first humans countenance, speech and the senses
norse_ve.notes: Snorri's Gylfaginning assigns to the third brother the gift of face, speech, hearing and sight to Askr and Embla (the gifts are distributed among the three).

norse_vili.name: with Odin and Vé slays Ymir and shapes the world
norse_vili.notes: One of the three sons of Borr who kill the frost-giant Ymir and build the world from his body (Gylfaginning).

norse_vili.name: gives the first humans will, motion and wit (his name means 'Will')
norse_vili.notes: Vili ('will') is named with Vé as co-creator; the brothers endow Askr and Embla with the inner faculties.

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning (Prose Edda), ch. 9; Lokasenna 26 (Poetic Edda)

norse_sigmund.name: alone can draw Odin's sword Gram from the tree Barnstokkr
norse_sigmund.notes: At his sister Signý's wedding a one-eyed stranger (Odin) thrusts a sword into Barnstokkr; only Sigmund can pull it free (Vǫlsunga saga ch. 3).

norse_sigrun.name: as a valkyrie rides air and sea and shields her chosen warrior in battle
norse_sigrun.notes: Helgakviða Hundingsbana: Sigrún and her valkyrie company ride over sky and sea to ward Helgi in the fight against Hǫðbroddr.

norse_sigrun.name: chooses Helgi as her husband against her father's betrothal
norse_sigrun.notes: Refusing the match to Hǫðbroddr, she seeks out Helgi Hundingsbani and weds him after he wins the battle of Frekastein.

norse_signy.name: engineers the destruction of Siggeir across years of patient revenge
norse_signy.notes: Vǫlsunga saga: Signý tests her sons, conceives Sinfjǫtli by her own brother Sigmund to breed an avenger of pure Vǫlsung blood, then dies in the burning of Siggeir's hall she helped contrive.

norse_signy.name: exchanges her shape with a sorceress to lie with Sigmund unrecognised
norse_signy.notes: By witchcraft she takes another woman's form to come unknown to her brother and beget Sinfjǫtli.

norse_volsung.name: is conceived by the fertility-apple Frigg sends to Rerir
norse_volsung.notes: Vǫlsunga saga: Rerir's queen eats the apple sent by Óðinn's messenger from Frigg and bears Vǫlsung after a long pregnancy; he is cut living from his dying mother.

norse_jormunrekkr.name: has Svanhild trampled by horses and Randvér hanged on a slander
norse_jormunrekkr.notes: Believing the charge that his wife Svanhild and his son Randvér betrayed him, Jǫrmunrekkr hangs Randvér and has Svanhild trodden to death by horses (Hamðismál; Vǫlsunga saga).

sources.reference: Hamðismál (Poetic Edda); Vǫlsunga saga ch. 42; Snorri, Skáldskaparmál

norse_idunn.name: the ash-wood casket (eski) holding the apples of youth

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda), ch. 86 on Iðunn-kennings

norse_jormungandr.name: world-poisoning venom that fills air and sea at Ragnarök

norse_nanna.name: the linen robe and finger-ring she sends from Hel to Frigg and Fulla

norse_surtr.name: the flaming sword brighter than the sun

sources.reference: Vǫluspá 52 (Poetic Edda); Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 4 and 51

norse_magni.name: Gullfaxi ('Golden-mane'), the horse of Hrungnir given him by Thor

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda), the Hrungnir episode

norse_magni.name: Mjǫllnir, the hammer he inherits after Ragnarök

norse_sigrun.name: the valkyrie's helm and byrnie reddened with blood she wears riding the air

norse_ragnar.name: the shaggy hair-breeches (loðbrók) boiled in pitch that ward off the dragon's venom

norse_sorli.name: the byrnie of the Jónakrssynir that iron could not bite

norse_idunn.gloss: keeper of the apples (the Æsir's age-old cure)

norse_jord.gloss: the Earth (a poetic name of Jǫrð, mother of Thor)

sources.reference: Ragnars saga loðbrókar; Saxo Grammaticus, Gesta Danorum bk. 9
Fáfnismál (Poetic Edda); Vǫlsunga saga; Snorri, Skáldskaparmál

norse_ymir.gloss: a byname of the primordial giant Ymir
a byname of Ymir (from whose skull/blood the dwarves were made)

sources.reference: Þjóðólfr of Hvinir, Haustlöng; Snorri, Skáldskaparmál
Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning and Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda)
Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (Prose Edda); Hárbarðsljóð 19 (Poetic Edda)

norse_njord.name: the toast to Njǫrðr and Freyr for plenty and peace at the sacrificial feast

term.value: Njarðar full ok Freys full til árs ok friðar
term.rom: Njarðar full ok Freys full til árs ok friðar

norse_njord.notes: At the blót the horn was drained to Njǫrðr and Freyr 'for good harvest and peace'; his name survives in Norwegian cult place-names such as Njarðarlǫg and Norderhov (Njarðar-hof, 'Njǫrðr's temple').

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Hákonar saga góða (Heimskringla), ch. 14

norse_thor.name: libation to the idol of Thor against plague and famine at the temple of Uppsala
norse_thor.cadence: in time of dearth or plague
norse_thor.notes: Adam of Bremen describes Thor enthroned in the centre of the Uppsala temple between Wodan and Fricco, holding a scepter; when plague or famine threatened, the offering went to Thor.

sources.reference: Adam of Bremen, Gesta Hammaburgensis ecclesiae pontificum, bk. 4 (Descriptio insularum aquilonis)

norse_tyr.name: offerings to Týr at his sacred groves and lakes
norse_tyr.notes: Týr's name is preserved in cult place-names such as Tislund ('Týr's grove') in Denmark; the lake Tissø ('Týr's lake') has yielded great quantities of deposited Viking-age weapons interpreted as offerings.

sources.reference: toponymy of Tislund and Tissø; cf. de Vries, Altgermanische Religionsgeschichte

attributes.name: the apples of immortality she bears
attributes.notes: Iðunn is figured cradling the apples that keep the gods young, her defining attribute.

attributes.name: the colossal serpent coiled round Midgard biting its own tail
attributes.notes: Jǫrmungandr lies in the sea encircling the world, gripping its tail in its mouth (Gylfaginning).

attributes.name: Thor's fishing of the serpent in Viking-age carving
attributes.notes: The serpent appears with Thor's fishing-line on the Altuna runestone (Uppland) and amid Ragnarök scenes on the Gosforth Cross (Cumbria).

attributes.name: the fire-giant wreathed in flame bearing a sun-bright sword
attributes.notes: Surtr comes from the south at Ragnarök with fire, his sword shining brighter than the sun, and burns the world (Vǫluspá; Gylfaginning).

sources.reference: Vǫluspá 52 (Poetic Edda); Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 4 and 51

attributes.name: the vast primordial frost-giant formed in the meeting of frost and fire
attributes.notes: Ymir takes shape from the rime of Élivágar where the cold of Niflheim meets the heat of Muspell (Gylfaginning).

sacredAnimals.name: Auðhumla, the primeval cow that nourished him

attributes.name: the great thick shoe with which he braces against Fenrir's jaw
attributes.notes: Víðarr's iconic attribute is the shoe made from all the leather-scraps men have cut from their shoes, by which he kills the wolf at Ragnarök (Gylfaginning).

sources.reference: Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning (Prose Edda), ch. 51; Skáldskaparmál
